messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'mercury-prod-dedicated' high GPU utilization (98%). Queue length >15, 503s observed for ~4m. Paging on-call.

sre_amy: I'm on call. joining. any customer impact details?

eng_jake: telemetry link: https://observability/redwood/mercury-prod-dedicated - GPU util 97-99% across nodes, avg queue 18, p99 latency 2.1s -> 503s on some requests. No OOMs. No preemption events.

prod_nina: Mercury (enterprise / VPC) is single-tenant dedicated pool. Autoscaling flagged: OFF per contract. Account needs approval to burst into shared capacity.

acct_sam: looping in me. pinged customer (Mercury SRE) 2m ago, waiting response. they said if we can restore service quickly they'd authorize emergency burst for 30m.

eng-infra_maya: We're ready to add 2 nodes but spin-up is ~8-10m. We can also enable short-lived burst to shared pools immediately if sales/legal ok.

sre_amy: Options: 1) approve emergency burst -> immediate capacity from shared (fast) 2) scale up dedicated nodes -> slower but isolated 3) throttle long-seq requests or route heavy models to quantized variant 4) enable graceful degradation -> return 429 for low-priority routes.

eng_jake: quick mitigation I can push: enable model fallback for large responses to 'mercury-small-quant' to reduce token compute. Patch in routing now (will affect quality slightly).

sre_amy: do that now, please. also what's impact window if we burst for 30m?

eng-infra_maya: Burst -> immediate capacity, should drop queue to <5 within 90s. Scale-up -> ~8-10m to be fully healthy.

acct_sam: Customer approved emergency burst for 30m. They asked we keep them in the loop. I have them on a call if needed.

ops_luis: I'm executing burst. running command:

```
redwoodctl pools burst --pool mercury-prod-dedicated --from shared --nodes 2 --duration 30m --reason "customer emergency - approved by acct_sam"
```

ops_luis: burst request submitted, control plane accepted. Allocating nodes now.

incident-bot: automation: burst allocation succeeded. 2 shared nodes attached to mercury-prod-dedicated. New capacity visible.

eng_jake: routing fallback pushed: long-seq -> mercury-small-quant. Monitoring.

sre_amy: observing metrics... queue length dropping.

eng_jake: p95 latency back to 350ms, queue ~3. no further 503s reported.

prod_nina: :white_check_mark: customer informed via acct_sam. They confirmed traffic normalizing.

acct_sam: Mercury SRE: "Seeing normal response now, thanks. Keep burst running and we'll decide if we want permanent autoscale later."

sre_amy: Great. Next steps: 1) keep burst for 30m as requested 2) start scale-up of 2 dedicated nodes in parallel to replace burst later. eng-infra_maya to kick off.

eng-infra_maya: scale-up command queued:

```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool mercury-prod-dedicated --add-nodes 2 --type p4 --async
```

eng-infra_maya: scale-up in progress. ETA healthy ~9m.

ops_luis: added a Canary rule to route 5% traffic to fallback variant to verify quality impact.

sre_amy: good. I'll keep monitoring and annotate incident. If scale-up finishes, we'll drain the shared burst nodes and end emergency burst early to reduce cross-tenant exposure.

eng_jake: noted. Will run a short smoke test on a few customer routes once new nodes are healthy.

incident-bot: paging cleared from on-call after mitigation (sre_amy). Incident status: active -> stabilizing. Update: burst will expire at +30m by default; manual end if scale completes successfully.

prod_nina: Post-incident action items before close: - review autoscale contract flag for Mercury - add a one-click emergency-burst playbook for account-managed tenants - improve fallback model testing matrix

acct_sam: I'll schedule a call with Mercury to discuss permanent autoscale and runbook updates. Thanks team.

sre_amy: dropping final check in 15m. currently p99 latency 480ms, queue 1. No errors. :thumbsup:

eng-infra_maya: new dedicated nodes reported healthy at +8m, starting traffic shift from shared.

ops_luis: draining shared nodes now. command:

```
redwoodctl pools drain --pool mercury-prod-dedicated --source shared --nodes 2
```

incident-bot: burst ended (manual). Shared nodes detached. Incident status: resolved -> postmortem pending.

sre_amy: resolved. I'll file the postmortem and include timelines, the redwoodctl commands used, and action items. Thanks everyone.
